title: Pin Oak: Ancient Pin Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: A North American swamp oak with a drooping crown and scarlet autumn colour. Haarlem's in Frederikspark was planted in the 1840s.
intro: Pin oak is a North American swamp species, native to wet bottomland from the Great Lakes down through the Mississippi valley, that reached European gardens at the start of the nineteenth century and became a Dutch park favourite decades later. The oldest here is an 1840s planting in Haarlem's Frederikspark; Apeldoorn's in the Oranjepark dates from the 1860s, Eindhoven's at Prinsenhof from around 1900, and Sittard's in the Stadspark from around 1910. It is easy to place once you have seen one. The lower branches sweep down toward the grass while the upper ones reach up, and the leaves are cut into narrow, bristle-tipped lobes far sharper than any native oak's. The name comes from the small pin-like stubs of dead branchlets along the trunk. It holds its scarlet October colour and its dead leaves well into winter, often the last oak in a park still dressed.
